title: Natural Disasters, Financial Shocks, and Human Capital
authors: Jess N. Cornaggia; Kimberly Rodgers Cornaggia; Han Xia
eligible_reason: The underlying design is a staggered binary exposure (students whose parents' county experiences a financially disruptive FEMA disaster, at student-specific terms, with never-treated students as controls; Sun-Abraham eventstudyinteract with cohort(dis_termstart_year) and control_cohort(never_treat) is reported). But no reported specification has unit (student) fixed effects: all regressions absorb groupid = school x term x course (course-section FE, i.e. calendar time interacted with school and course) or groupid2 = that group x student origin state, plus field-of-study FE, and add student-level covariates ($control1-$control3: female white ln_age parentdegree numcollege bach ln_family_income per_poverty). The event-study versions interact these FE and covariates with relative time (distance_cat). In addition the BPS:12/17 data are restricted-use (NCES license) and no data are shipped, so nothing can be re-estimated.
design_notes: Code: 2.Analyses/8.Tables&Figures.do (1,414 lines) with Controls.do and Drop.do; intermediate builds in subfolders 1-7. Unit of observation: student x course (grades, withdraw ratio, STEM ratio) or student x term/year panels (family finance, hours, loans). Treatment: student_dis = 1 if student_dis_duration_sum>=1 in that term (1.Baseline/Analyses.do lines 164-165), i.e. the student's family county has an active financially disruptive disaster; student_dis_all = ever treated; never_treat = (id_treat_id==0 & id_treat_id_all==0) in 7.Dynamic. FE: groupid = group(schoolid termstart_year termstart_mon courseid); groupid2 = group(groupid student_st); field17. Weights pw=weight1 (BPS sample weights). Cluster: student_fips genid (two-way). Static regressions: reghdfe gpa student_dis $controlK [pw=weight1], a(groupid field17) etc. (lines 459-547, Table 3). Dynamic: reghdfe gpa id_treat_id##ib360.distance_cat distance_cat##($control3i), a(groupid2##distance_cat field17##distance_cat) (line 1341, Figure 1); eventstudyinteract outcome time1 time3 time4 time5, cohort(dis_termstart_year or dis_academic_year or treat_academic_half) control_cohort(never_treat) covariates(... distance_cat##controls) absorb(groupid2##distance_cat field17##distance_cat) (lines 1131-1290). Falsification (Figure 2) uses EFC=0/independent students.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Cohorts defined by dis_termstart_year / dis_academic_year (disasters 2011-2018, so several annual cohorts); exact counts are suppressed by IES disclosure rules and the data are not shipped.

specs.sample_condition: analyses_treat after Drop.do (FAFSA filers; drop treated students with zero EFC)

specs.exclusion_reason: no unit FE; covariates interacted with relative time; data not available

specs.exclusion_reason: no unit FE; covariates; data not available

data_access: proprietary (BPS:12/17 restricted-use license from NCES/IES; no data shipped; variable names redacted per IES rules)
screener_notes: Code only; even the variable names are described as redacted/concealed to satisfy IES rules. The design is a staggered binary shock with never-treated controls and a reported Sun-Abraham estimator, but the estimating equations compare treated and untreated students within course sections (no student FE) and always include student covariates, so no TWFE counterpart in the protocol's sense is reported. Re-screen only if the article text shows a student-FE panel specification.
hand_check_nov4: Not a near-miss: no unit (student) fixed effects in any specification. The record and the article tables (course-semester FE, field-of-study FE, family-state FE; no student FE) show treated and untreated students compared within course sections with student covariates, so the regressions are not TWFE (PROTOCOL 5b ruling for designs without unit or treated-group FE, mnsc.2024.05301). BPS restricted-use data not shipped. near_miss stays false; eligible_design true is a legacy coding.
